description: General spacecraft-wide fault knowledge base covering attitude control, onboard computing, and cascading multi-subsystem anomalies not specific to battery/comms/thermal.

faults.name: Reaction Wheel Failure / Increased Friction
faults.telemetry_signature: Gradual increase in wheel motor current for a given commanded rate (contextual anomaly), sometimes followed by a sudden point anomaly where the wheel stops responding entirely despite full motor voltage.
likely_causes: Bearing degradation from loss of lubrication
Increased mechanical friction in the wheel assembly over mission lifetime
Wheel driver electronics fault (e.g. improper H-bridge switching bypassing a motor winding)
recommended_actions: Monitor wheel friction/current trend to catch degradation before hard failure
Switch to a redundant reaction wheel or fall back to a reduced-wheel control mode if available
If only one axis is affected, consider gyroless/reduced-actuator attitude determination modes

real_world_example.summary: In July 2012, Kepler's reaction wheel assembly 2 (RWA2) stopped spinning entirely. The mission continued on 3 wheels, but RWA4 later developed increased friction and permanently failed, suspending science data collection until a revised control mode was developed.

faults.name: Attitude Control Fault / Tumble
faults.telemetry_signature: Rapid, large-magnitude deviation across multiple attitude-related channels simultaneously (angular rate, pointing error) - typically a sharp point anomaly at onset, frequently the root cause behind subsequent power/thermal/comms anomalies.
likely_causes: Gyro discrepancy leading to an incorrect fault diagnosis and switch to a faulty backup gyro
Vehicle attitude rates exceeding what onboard reaction wheels can control
Propulsion system valve issue during a trajectory correction maneuver
recommended_actions: Cross-check independent attitude sensors (gyros, star trackers, sun sensors) before committing to a diagnosis
Trigger safe mode to stop the tumble using thrusters or reduced-actuator control
Treat any subsequent power, thermal, or comms anomaly as potentially downstream of this root cause

real_world_example.summary: A gyro discrepancy led operators to misdiagnose and disable the wrong gyro; the spacecraft began wobbling, reached 7 RPM spin, and contact was lost within 5 minutes. Recovery required activating the transmitter and changing the battery charging strategy over several days.
real_world_example.source: AEROSPACE REPORT NO. TOR-2009(8591)-14, Effective Fault Management Guidelines

faults.name: Flight Computer Reset / Software Fault
faults.telemetry_signature: Sudden gap or discontinuity across most/all telemetry channels simultaneously, followed by a step-change back to nominal-looking values after reboot - a distinctive whole-system point anomaly.
likely_causes: Unexpected flight computer reset from a software exception or watchdog timeout
Single-event upset (radiation-induced bit flip) corrupting a critical memory location
RAM error in a subsystem such as a star tracker
recommended_actions: Confirm successful reboot and re-verify subsystem health checklist before resuming normal operations
Review onboard event logs / watchdog records to identify the triggering condition
If radiation-related, note the event for space-weather correlation (was a solar event active at the time?)

real_world_example.summary: TESS entered safe mode after an unexpected flight computer reset (10-13 Oct 2022) and recovered. Around the same period, Orion experienced a RAM error in its star tracker system during Artemis I.
real_world_example.source: Spacecraft Anomalies and Failures Workshop 2023, NASA

faults.name: Unrecovered Loss of Contact (Unknown Root Cause)
faults.telemetry_signature: Total telemetry dropout with no subsequent recovery - distinguishing feature is the absence of any partial-signal or degraded-but-present pattern seen in a typical LOS event.
likely_causes: Unknown / unconfirmed - may be any combination of power, attitude, thermal, or comms failure without sufficient final telemetry to diagnose
Catastrophic single-point failure in a non-redundant critical system
Complete loss of power preventing any fault-protection response
recommended_actions: Review the last received telemetry across ALL subsystems (not just the channel that triggered the anomaly) for any leading indicator
Check space-weather logs for a coincident solar event
Document as an unresolved anomaly; avoid overfitting a root-cause explanation to limited final data

real_world_example.summary: NASA's ICON mission lost contact on 25 Nov 2022 and had not been recovered as of the reporting workshop in Feb 2023, with the cause listed as unknown - illustrating that not every anomaly resolves to a clean diagnosis.
real_world_example.source: Spacecraft Anomalies and Failures Workshop 2023, NASA

faults.name: Gyro Drift / Bias Error
faults.telemetry_signature: Slow, accumulating divergence between gyro-derived attitude and an independent reference (star tracker/sun sensor) - a contextual anomaly growing over time rather than a sudden jump.
likely_causes: Gyro bias drift with age/temperature
Radiation-induced sensor degradation
Insufficient recalibration against independent attitude references
recommended_actions: Increase frequency of star-tracker-based attitude recalibration
Trend bias drift rate to predict when correction will next be needed
Switch to a redundant gyro if drift exceeds acceptable bounds

faults.name: Star Tracker False Lock / Blinding
faults.telemetry_signature: Sudden loss of valid star tracker attitude solution correlated with a bright object (Sun, Moon, Earth limb) entering the field of view - a point anomaly with a clear geometric trigger.
likely_causes: Direct or near-field sunlight/moonlight entering the tracker's field of view
Stray light from a nearby spacecraft structure
False star pattern match during a bright-body transit
recommended_actions: Cross-check against attitude/pointing telemetry to confirm a bright-body transit caused the loss
Rely on gyro-only attitude propagation until the tracker reacquires after the transit
Adjust future pointing profiles to avoid known blinding geometries if the event is predictable

faults.name: Solar Array Deployment Failure
faults.telemetry_signature: Deployment status telemetry never confirms full deployment, or power output stays well below expected post-deployment levels - a point anomaly tied to a specific one-time deployment event.
likely_causes: Mechanical jamming of the deployment mechanism
Pyrotechnic or motor-driven release device failure
Thermal binding preventing full panel travel
recommended_actions: Re-attempt the deployment command sequence if retry is supported
Thermally cycle the mechanism (sun exposure change via attitude) to relieve possible binding
Reassess power budget and mission plan around reduced available power if redeployment fails

faults.name: Propulsion Valve Stiction
faults.telemetry_signature: Thruster firing produces less than commanded impulse, or valve position telemetry lags the command - a point anomaly tied to specific commanded burns rather than continuous drift.
likely_causes: Mechanical stiction in the valve mechanism
Contamination in the propellant line affecting valve seating
Cold temperature increasing mechanical friction in the valve
recommended_actions: Cross-check valve temperature against its qualified operating range before the next burn
Command a valve exercise cycle to attempt to free stiction
Adjust burn duration/planning to compensate for reduced impulse if stiction persists

faults.name: Software Watchdog Timeout Loop
faults.telemetry_signature: Repeated flight computer resets occurring at a regular interval - a recurring point anomaly pattern rather than a single isolated reset.
likely_causes: A software task hanging and triggering the watchdog repeatedly after each reset
Corrupted configuration data causing the same fault to recur after reboot
A hardware fault intermittently triggering the watchdog condition
recommended_actions: Review onboard logs immediately after each reset to identify the hanging task before the next timeout occurs
Load a known-good configuration/software image if corruption is suspected
Escalate to a safe/minimal operating mode to break the reset loop if it continues

faults.name: Memory Bit-Flip (Single-Event Upset) in Non-Critical Register
faults.telemetry_signature: A single telemetry value briefly reads an implausible, physically-impossible value for exactly one sample before returning to normal - a very short, isolated point anomaly.
likely_causes: Cosmic ray or energetic particle strike flipping a memory bit
Radiation environment intensity increase (e.g. during a solar event)
Non-radiation-hardened memory location in a non-critical subsystem
recommended_actions: Confirm the value returned to normal on the very next sample before treating it as a real physical event
Check space-weather data for a coincident solar/radiation event
No corrective action typically needed for a single isolated sample; flag only if the pattern recurs frequently

faults.name: Sensor Harness Chafing / Intermittent Connection
faults.telemetry_signature: A sensor channel intermittently drops out or reads noise for brief periods, often correlated with spacecraft vibration/thermal-flex events - a recurring point anomaly pattern rather than a continuous fault.
likely_causes: Wiring harness insulation wear (chafing) at a flex point or vibration-prone location
Connector pin degradation causing an intermittent contact
Thermal expansion/contraction stressing a marginal connection
recommended_actions: Correlate dropout timing with known vibration events (thruster firings, mechanism operation) or thermal transitions
Cross-check with a redundant sensor if available while the intermittent fault is investigated
Document the pattern for post-mission root-cause analysis, since in-flight harness repair isn't possible

faults.name: Relay Contact Welding
faults.telemetry_signature: A commanded relay/switch operation fails to change state - the corresponding status telemetry stays stuck at its prior value despite the command being sent, a clear point anomaly at a specific command event.
likely_causes: Contact welding from an over-current switching event
Mechanical failure of the relay actuator
Command not actually reaching the relay due to a wiring fault
recommended_actions: Verify the command was actually received (check command-echo telemetry) before assuming a relay hardware fault
Attempt the command again in case of a one-time transient issue
Switch to a redundant relay/path if the stuck state is confirmed and persistent

faults.name: Power Distribution Unit Overcurrent Trip
faults.telemetry_signature: A specific load's current draw spikes sharply just before that load's telemetry goes to zero (breaker/fuse trip) - a sharp point anomaly with a clear before/after signature.
likely_causes: Short circuit or fault developing within the affected load
Inrush current exceeding the breaker's threshold at power-on
Breaker/fuse threshold set too conservatively for normal operating current
recommended_actions: Do not immediately re-close the breaker without reviewing the current spike magnitude and duration
Check whether the trip coincided with a power-on event (inrush) versus continuous operation (possible fault)
Escalate to ground review before re-enabling if a genuine short circuit is suspected

faults.name: GPS/Navigation Solution Divergence
faults.telemetry_signature: Onboard-computed position/velocity solution slowly diverges from ground-tracked orbital elements - a slow contextual anomaly in a derived navigation value.
likely_causes: GPS receiver clock drift
Reduced satellite visibility/geometry affecting solution quality
Onboard orbit propagation model not being refreshed with recent ground tracking data
recommended_actions: Cross-check onboard navigation solution against latest ground-tracked orbital elements
Command an onboard state vector update/refresh if divergence exceeds tolerance
Investigate GPS receiver health if divergence persists after a refresh

faults.name: Payload Instrument Calibration Drift
faults.telemetry_signature: Instrument output for a known reference target/calibration source slowly shifts from its expected value - a slow contextual anomaly in a science/payload channel rather than a spacecraft-bus health channel.
likely_causes: Detector aging affecting response characteristics
Optical/mechanical component degradation within the instrument
Accumulated radiation dose affecting sensor response
recommended_actions: Schedule a calibration observation against a known reference target to quantify the drift
Apply a calibration correction factor to science data processing if drift is well-characterized
Flag for instrument team review if drift rate is accelerating

faults.name: Magnetorquer Saturation
faults.telemetry_signature: Commanded magnetic dipole moment repeatedly hits its maximum limit without achieving the desired attitude/momentum correction - a contextual anomaly visible as sustained command-saturation rather than a hardware failure.
likely_causes: Reaction wheel momentum has built up beyond what magnetorquers can desaturate given current orbital position
Weak local magnetic field geometry at the current orbital location limiting torque authority
Higher-than-expected disturbance torque requiring more desaturation capacity than planned
recommended_actions: Allow more time/orbits for desaturation rather than treating this as a single-event fault
Cross-check reaction wheel momentum telemetry to confirm this is a desaturation-capacity issue, not a magnetorquer hardware fault
Consider adjusting attitude profile to reduce disturbance torque accumulation if saturation is frequent

faults.name: Onboard Clock Drift
faults.telemetry_signature: A slow, accumulating offset between onboard time and ground reference time - a slow contextual anomaly best seen in time-tagged telemetry correlation, not any single channel.
likely_causes: Oscillator aging affecting the onboard clock's frequency stability
Temperature-induced clock rate variation
Missed or delayed periodic time-synchronization uplinks
recommended_actions: Command a time-synchronization update to correct the offset
Trend drift rate to determine appropriate resync frequency going forward
Review any time-critical commands executed during the drift period for potential timing errors

faults.name: Redundant Unit Cross-Strapping Fault
faults.telemetry_signature: Switching to a redundant/backup unit does not fully restore expected functionality - a point anomaly discovered specifically during a failover event, not during normal primary-unit operation.
likely_causes: Cross-strap wiring fault affecting the backup path specifically
Backup unit itself degraded from long-term unpowered dormancy
Configuration mismatch between primary and backup unit settings
recommended_actions: Verify backup unit configuration matches expected settings before further troubleshooting
Check cross-strap-specific telemetry/status if available, separate from the unit's own health telemetry
Document as a redundancy-path issue distinct from a simple unit failure, since it affects failover reliability specifically

faults.name: EMI/EMC Interference Between Subsystems
faults.telemetry_signature: A sensitive channel shows noise or brief anomalous readings correlated with another subsystem's operating schedule (e.g. a specific instrument or mechanism powering on) - a recurring contextual anomaly with a clear timing correlation.
likely_causes: Insufficient electromagnetic shielding/isolation between subsystems
Shared power bus noise coupling between loads
Unexpected harmonic interference from a specific subsystem's switching frequency
recommended_actions: Correlate anomaly timing precisely against other subsystems' operating schedules to identify the interference source
Adjust operational timing to avoid simultaneous operation of the interfering subsystems where possible
Escalate to EMC engineering review if interference is structural and can't be avoided operationally

faults.name: Command Uplink Buffer Corruption
faults.telemetry_signature: A stored command sequence executes incorrectly or partially at its scheduled time, despite having been correctly uplinked and acknowledged earlier - a point anomaly at execution time, not at uplink time.
likely_causes: Memory corruption of the stored command buffer between uplink and execution
A subsequent command inadvertently overwriting part of the stored sequence
Radiation-induced bit flip in the command storage location
recommended_actions: Compare the executed command sequence against the originally uplinked sequence to characterize the corruption
Re-uplink the sequence closer to its execution time in the future to reduce the exposure window
Flag for review if this is a recurring pattern rather than an isolated event
